title: Declared validation never runs Astro or TypeScript diagnostics
reasoning: The package declares a strict Astro TypeScript configuration and installs @astrojs/check, but no package script exposes or chains an Astro/TypeScript check. The only automated validation script builds and runs Playwright visual tests, so type diagnostics are not part of the package's declared review or release path.
reproduction: Add a type-only error that Astro/Vite can transpile, then run the declared validation command `bun run test:visual`; there is no package script step that invokes `astro check`, `astro-check`, or `tsc`.
recommendation: Add a `check` or `typecheck` script, for example `astro check`, and include it in the normal validation path or CI before visual tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked Playwright tests verify selected rendered pages, print behavior, screenshots, and PDF page counts; they do not invoke the installed Astro checker or TypeScript compiler diagnostics.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add CI/package validation that runs `bun run check` before `bun run test:visual`, and keep a documented command for contributors to run the same checks locally.
minimumFixScope: Update `package.json` scripts and, if applicable, the documented validation command.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist, but the script evidence has changed: package.json now declares "check": "astro check" at line 12 and "test": "bun run check && bun run test:visual" at line 13, while "test:visual" remains build-plus-Playwright at line 14. @astrojs/check is still installed and tsconfig.json still extends astro/tsconfigs/strict. `bun run check` executed Astro diagnostics successfully with 0 errors. `bun run test` also proved the normal validation path invokes `astro check` before visual tests; it failed later only because the Playwright Chromium executable is missing from the local cache, not because Astro/TypeScript diagnostics are absent.
